name: Accordion
summary: Use an accordion to let users reveal and hide related sections when showing all of the content at once would make a page difficult to scan.
whenToUse: Use for several related sections when users need only some of the content and can understand each section from its heading.
Consider simplifying or splitting the page before introducing an accordion.
Use expanded sections sparingly when a section is likely to be needed immediately.
whenNotToUse: Do not hide information that most users need to complete the current task.
Do not use an accordion as a substitute for a clear page structure or a sequence of service steps.
Do not use it for content that users need to compare across sections at the same time.

anatomy.name: Accordion container
anatomy.description: A uniquely identified container carries govuk-accordion and data-module="govuk-accordion".

anatomy.name: Section
anatomy.description: Each repeated section contains one header and one content region.

anatomy.name: Section heading
anatomy.description: A heading at the correct document level contains the section-button hook and a unique ID.

anatomy.name: Section content
anatomy.description: The content region has a unique ID associated with the same accordion and section position.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: Related sections start collapsed after enhancement while remaining visible without JavaScript.

variants.name: Expanded section
variants.use: A section whose content should be open when the enhanced component first appears.

behaviour: Initialise the official govuk-accordion module from GOV.UK Frontend.
Without JavaScript, all section content remains visible under ordinary headings.
With JavaScript, GOV.UK Frontend creates disclosure controls, state text, and show-all behaviour.
Container, heading, and content IDs must be unique on the page.
accessibility: Choose heading elements that preserve the page's logical heading hierarchy.
Section headings must identify the content clearly when read independently.
Do not hand-build the enhanced button and ARIA state; initialise the official module from the documented base markup.
Do not hide the unenhanced content before GOV.UK Frontend confirms JavaScript support.
content: Place the information users need to decide whether to expand a section in its heading or optional summary.
Avoid repeating the same opening words across every heading when distinctive wording is available.
